title: Landscape Construction: Irrigation Practices
description: Methods and materials used in the irrigation of ornamental landscapes. Selection of materials and operational theory of irrigation equipment. Installation techniques for sprinkler and drip irrigation systems. Water conservation features and maintenance of irrigation systems.
outcomes: Identify the parts of an irrigation system (pipes and fittings, sprinkler heads, valves, backflow preventers, drip systems, and controllers).
Program an irrigation time clock (controller) correctly.
objectives: Compare irrigation systems used in various settings.
Analyze a site for irrigation needs.
Select the correct irrigation equipment for spray and drip irrigation systems.
Demonstrate maintenance skills for an irrigation system.
content: Gallons per minute (GPM) and pounds per square inch (PSI)
Central control of parks and municipal settings
Model Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance (MWELO) in California
Recycled and untreated water in irrigation
Gray water use in irrigation systems
Secondary or tertiary treated sewage water
lab: Copper and solvent welding lab: Hands-on instruction in welding of copper pipe and fittings, solvent welding of plastic pipe, and making pipe and irrigation component connections for threaded fittings.
Spray head and rotor lab: Field installation and adjustment of a variety of sprinkler products.
Controller programming lab: Individual instruction on the programming of irrigation controllers, covering standard solid-state controllers, ET based controllers, and central control systems.
Drip irrigation lab: Installation of drip systems including standard PE flexible lines, drip heads, and in-line drip emitter systems.
Valve troubleshooting lab: Modular lab covers all the common problems that irrigation professionals may encounter when valves malfunction in the landscape.
Irrigation system installation lab: One or more labs whereby students install an irrigation system.
